title: Simple English: every explainer can carry a second, plainer version
subtitle: What the toggle changes on a page, what it leaves alone, and how the writing is checked

sections.title: Readers can switch any explainer to plainer words
sections.label: The verdict
sections.text: A section can hold a second version of its prose. A toggle named Simple English shows that version in place of the normal one, and the page remembers the choice.
points: The page opens in normal text. Print and a page with no script show normal text too.
Code, commands, numbers and answers never change when the toggle flips.
A validate step warns when the plain version breaks a writing rule.

simple.title: Readers can switch an explainer to plain words
simple.text: A section can hold a second, plainer version of its text. The Simple English button shows it. The page keeps your choice.
points: The page starts in normal text. Print shows normal text too.
Code, commands, numbers and answers stay the same.
A check warns you when the plain text breaks a writing rule.

sections.title: The toggle swaps prose and nothing else
sections.label: What changes
sections.text:
Ten section types can carry a `simple` field: the summary, text, cards, risks, steps, timeline, comparison, note, details and table sections. A field left out of `simple` keeps its normal text, so a writer only rewrites what needs it.

Contents labels and section ids stay the same in both views, so every link keeps working.

simple.title: The button changes the words and nothing else
simple.text:
Ten kinds of section can hold a `simple` version. If you leave a field out, the normal words stay. You only rewrite what needs it.

The contents list and the links stay the same in both views.

sections.title: Four writing rules keep the plain version plain
sections.label: The rules

items.title: Short sentences
items.text: Twenty-five words at most, and twenty in a step.

items.title: One idea at a time
items.text: A paragraph holds six sentences at most.

items.title: Common words
items.text: Write `use` and `before`, not their wordy forms.

items.title: Say who acts
items.text: Prefer "the build ran" over "the build was run".
Use 25 words or fewer. In a step, use 20 or fewer.
Put six sentences or fewer in a paragraph.
Pick the short word, such as `use` or `before`.

sections.title: Adding the plain version takes four steps
sections.label: How to add it

items.title: Write the normal text first
items.text: Finish each section the usual way, with its title and prose.

items.title: Add a simple field
items.text: Copy the prose fields into `simple` and rewrite them with the four rules.

items.title: Run validate
items.text: It prints warnings for sentences that run long or use a wordy phrase.

items.title: Open the page
items.text: Press the Simple English button and read both versions.

items.title: Add a simple field
items.text: Copy the text fields into `simple`. Then rewrite them.

items.title: Run validate
items.text: It warns you about long sentences and wordy phrases.

items.title: Open the page
items.text: Press Simple English. Read both versions.

sections.title: A simple field sits beside the text
sections.label: Example

sections.title: Two things can still go wrong
sections.label: Risks

items.risk: The two versions drift apart when only one is edited.
items.mitigation: Validate warns when a section has no simple text on a page that has some.
They catch long sentences and wordy phrases. A person still reads the result.

items.risk: One version gets edited and the other does not.
items.mitigation: Validate warns when a section has no simple text.
They catch long sentences and wordy phrases. A person still reads the page.
